quote: Target **Python 3.10+**.
statement: In all Python files, code must target Python 3.10+ (may use 3.10 syntax, must not rely on features newer than the supported minimum).

quote: Follow [PEP 8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/) style conventions.
statement: In all Python files, code should follow PEP 8 style conventions (naming, whitespace, layout).

quote: Use clear, descriptive names and add docstrings to public functions/classes.
statement: In all Python files, public functions and classes must have docstrings.

quote: Use clear, descriptive names and add docstrings to public functions/classes.
statement: In all Python files, identifiers should be clear and descriptive.

quote: Prefer small, readable functions over large, complex ones.
statement: In all Python files, functions should be small and readable rather than large and complex.

quote: Keep dependencies minimal; discuss new runtime dependencies in an issue first.
statement: Across the project, new runtime dependencies should be kept minimal and discussed before being added.

quote: Add or update tests for any behavior you change.
statement: Any change to behavior must be accompanied by added or updated tests.

quote: **Format:** Use Google-style docstrings
statement: In veritas-reason/veritasreason/**, docstrings must use Google style (Args:, Returns:, Raises:, Example: sections).

quote: | **mypy** | Type checking              | `mypy veritasreason/`          |
statement: In veritas-reason/veritasreason/**, code must type-check under mypy (type hints on functions).

quote: | **flake8** | Style enforcement          | `flake8 veritasreason/ tests/` |
statement: In veritas-reason/veritasreason/** and veritas-reason/tests/**, code must pass flake8 style enforcement.

quote: Improve code quality (add type hints, docstrings, improve error messages)
statement: In veritas-reason/veritasreason/**, functions should carry type hints and docstrings and raise informative error messages.

quote: - Add tests for new features
statement: In veritas-reason, new features must be accompanied by tests under veritas-reason/tests/.

quote: **Coverage goal:** 80% minimum, 90%+ for critical modules
statement: In veritas-reason, test coverage should be at least 80%, and 90%+ for critical modules.

quote: - [ ] Code follows project style (Black, isort, flake8)
statement: In veritas-reason, code must follow the project style enforced by Black, isort and flake8.
In veritas-reason, custom ingestors must subclass veritasreason.ingest.BaseIngestor and implement ingest(source) returning a list of document dicts.
In veritas-reason, custom extractors must subclass veritasreason.semantic_extract.BaseExtractor and implement extract(text) returning a list of entity dicts.

quote: **Pluggability** — extend any layer without modifying core code. Custom ingestors, extractors, validators, and exporters all follow the same base class pattern.
statement: In veritas-reason, custom ingestors, extractors, validators and exporters must follow the base-class pattern (subclass the module's Base* class) rather than modifying core code.

quote: **Modularity** — every component can be used standalone. Import only what you need; the framework never forces a full stack.
statement: In veritas-reason/veritasreason/**, each module must be usable standalone and must not force importing the full stack.

quote: **Configuration over convention** — centralized config with environment variable overrides for deployment flexibility.
statement: In veritas-reason/veritasreason/**, configuration should go through the centralized config with environment variable overrides.

quote: **Provenance by default** — lineage tracking is built into graph construction, not bolted on. Every node traces back to a source document.
statement: In veritas-reason/veritasreason/kg/** graph construction, every created node must carry provenance tracing back to its source document.

quote: - id: check-docstring-first
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, code must not appear before the module docstring (the docstring must come first).

quote: - id: debug-statements
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, code must not contain debugger imports or calls (pdb, ipdb, breakpoint()).

quote:
- id: name-tests-test
  args: ['--pytest-test-first']
statement: In veritas-reason test directories, test files must be named test_*.py.

quote: flake8 args: ['--max-line-length=88', ...]
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, lines must not exceed 88 characters (flake8 E501).

quote: flake8 args: ['--extend-ignore=E203,W503'] (E203)
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, flake8 E203 (whitespace before ':') is not enforced.

quote: flake8 args: ['--extend-ignore=E203,W503'] (W503)
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, flake8 W503 (line break before binary operator) is not enforced.

quote: - id: python-check-blanket-noqa
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, `# noqa` comments must name specific codes; blanket `# noqa` must not be used.

quote: - id: python-check-mock-methods
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, code must not call non-existent mock assertion methods (e.g. assert_called_once, not_called, called_once_with misspellings).

quote: - id: python-no-eval
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, code must not use the builtin eval().

quote: - id: python-no-log-warn
statement: In veritas-reason Python files, code must not call the deprecated logger .warn(); use .warning() instead.

quote:
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"
statement: In submission/veritasgraph_rag/**, ruff is configured with line-length 100 and target py310 (no explicit rule selection; defaults only).

quote: The key idea: **each block talks through a defined interface**, so any one can be replaced without touching the others.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot/app/**, components must communicate only through their defined interfaces, not each other's internals.

quote: **Do NOT touch:** channel layer, case service, fusion logic — they read the category and labels generically from the KG.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, the channel layer, app/case_service.py and app/fusion.py must not hardcode incident categories or CV labels; they read them generically from the knowledge graph.

quote: **Do NOT touch:** orchestrator, fusion, KG — they consume the contract, not the model internals.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, app/orchestrator.py, app/fusion.py and app/knowledge_graph.py must consume CV results only via the CV service contract (app/cv_service.py) and must not depend on model internals (e.g. import ultralytics/YOLO directly).

quote: | Move to a hosted VLM API (GPT-4o / Gemini) | Implement an adapter that maps the API response into the contract above |
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, any new CV/VLM backend must be wrapped in an adapter that returns the CV contract shape ({detections: [{label, confidence, bbox}], model}).

quote: **Swap the engine** (e.g. Neo4j → Cosmos DB Gremlin → RDF): implement a new adapter behind the grounding service's repository interface
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, knowledge-graph engines must be implemented as adapters behind the KnowledgeRepository interface (classify, route, findSimilar, getPolicy); callers must not depend on the engine directly.

quote: **Touch:** add a channel adapter that translates the channel's messages into the orchestrator's canonical request
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, each channel must be a channel adapter that translates messages into the orchestrator's canonical request ({userId, text, attachments, channel}).

quote: **Do NOT touch:** orchestrator, KG, CV, case service — they are channel-agnostic. Only handle channel-specific limits at the edge
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, app/orchestrator.py, app/knowledge_graph.py, app/cv_service.py and app/case_service.py must not contain channel-specific logic; channel limits are handled only in edge adapters.

quote:
**Touch:** implement a connector behind the **External Connectors** interface:
```
CorroborationSource:
  supports(incidentType, location) -> bool
  fetch(location, timeWindow) -> Evidence[]
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, external corroboration sources must implement the CorroborationSource interface with supports(incidentType, location) and fetch(location, timeWindow).

quote: corroboration is **optional by design** — if the source is down, fusion must still produce a (lower-confidence) result.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot/app/fusion.py, failure of a corroboration source must be handled so fusion still returns a (capped, lower-confidence) result instead of raising.

quote: Fusion combines signals into one score. Keep the weights and thresholds in **config**, not code, so tuning needs no redeploy.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot/app/fusion.py, fusion weights, thresholds and caps must be read from config and must not be hardcoded in code.

quote:
**Touch:** implement the case-sink interface used by the Case Registration Service:
```
CaseSink:
  create(case, evidenceBundle) -> caseId
  updateStatus(caseId, status) -> void
  findExisting(location, type, window) -> Case[]
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, case-management targets must be adapters implementing the CaseSink interface (create, updateStatus, findExisting).

quote: Swap the adapter; keep the retry/outbox behavior for resilience
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot/app/case_service.py, case-sink writes must keep retry/outbox behavior so outages persist cases locally and retry.

quote: **Do NOT touch:** orchestrator, CV, fusion — they call `CaseSink`, not the vendor SDK directly.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, app/orchestrator.py, app/cv_service.py and app/fusion.py must call CaseSink and must not import or call case-management vendor SDKs (ServiceNow, Dynamics 365) directly.

quote: **Change data before code.** Categories, departments, SLAs, and thresholds are data/config — prefer editing those over writing new logic.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, categories, departments, SLAs and thresholds should live in data/config rather than code logic.

quote: **Keep evidence auditable.** Any new signal or model must still write its output to the evidence bundle + audit log.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, every signal or model must write its output to the evidence bundle and the audit log.

quote: **Preserve graceful degradation.** New external dependencies must be optional; the system should never hard-fail because a corroboration source is offline.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, external dependencies must be optional and their failures must be caught so the system never hard-fails when a corroboration source is offline.

quote: If you *must* change a contract, update it in one place and version it.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, component contracts must be defined in one place and versioned when changed.

quote: **Grounded, not guessed.** Citizen-facing answers must come from a knowledge graph of real policies/departments/SLAs so the bot never invents rules.
statement: In municipality-incident-chatbot, citizen-facing answers must be grounded in knowledge-graph data and must not be produced from ungrounded LLM output.
